title: Rotate an SDDC Manager credential without stranding the old secret
prompt:
Platform engineering rotates SDDC Manager service credentials while automation is still calling the estate with the secret that is being replaced. A rotation must never be submitted while a caller can still hold the retired secret, and a replacement must never be handed to callers until SDDC Manager has confirmed it. Complete `VcfCredentialRotation/VcfCredentialRotation.psm1`.

Read protected `docs/contract.json` and `docs/official_sources.json` first. The contract was projected directly from `specifications/sddc-manager/sddc-manager-openapi.json` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository, at the immutable VCF 9.0 commit recorded in both files for tag `9.0.0.0`. That specification file is the wire authority: not a rendered documentation page, and not the `9.1.0.0` revision of the same file. The operationIds in scope are exactly `createToken`, `getCredentials`, `updateOrRotatePasswords`, `getCredentialsTask`, `retryCredentialsTask`, `cancelCredentialsTask`, and `getCredential`.

VCF PowerCLI is an environment prerequisite: `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.SddcManager` 13.5.0.25380678 or later is already installed. Every request must be issued by that genuine SDK, through `Invoke-VcfGetCredentials`, `Invoke-VcfUpdateOrRotatePasswords`, `Invoke-VcfGetCredentialsTask`, `Invoke-VcfRetryCredentialsTask`, `Invoke-VcfCancelCredentialsTask` and `Invoke-VcfGetCredential`, with the request payload built by `Initialize-VcfBaseCredential`, `Initialize-VcfResourceCredentials` and `Initialize-VcfCredentialsUpdateSpec`. Do not install, download, copy, generate, vendor, intercept or replace any VMware module, SDK assembly, binding or OpenAPI file, and do not reach the network with `Invoke-RestMethod`, `Invoke-WebRequest`, `HttpClient`, `WebClient`, raw sockets, `Start-Process`, `curl` or `wget`. The caller connects the SDK and passes the resulting server object in `-Server`; the module never authenticates by itself.

Export exactly one function and keep the supplied signature:

`Invoke-VcfCredentialRotation -Server <object> -ResourceType <string> -ResourceName <string> -Username <string> -CredentialType <string> [-AccountType <string>] -DrainAction <scriptblock> -PublishAction <scriptblock> [-DrainLimit <int>] [-DrainIntervalSeconds <int>] [-PollLimit <int>] [-PollIntervalSeconds <int>] [-SleepAction <scriptblock>]`

`DrainLimit` defaults to 10, `DrainIntervalSeconds` to 2, `PollLimit` to 60 and `PollIntervalSeconds` to 5. Reject a blank `ResourceType`, `ResourceName`, `Username`, `CredentialType` or supplied `AccountType`, a `DrainLimit` or `PollLimit` below 1, and a negative interval, all before any request. When `SleepAction` is supplied, invoke it with the number of seconds instead of sleeping; otherwise use `Start-Sleep`.

Perform exactly this workflow.

1. Identify the credential with `getCredentials`, filtering on the resource name and resource type, plus the account type when `-AccountType` was bound. Select the single returned element whose `username` and `credentialType` match case-sensitively; a different account or a different credential type on the same resource is not a match. Fail if the match count is not exactly one, or if the matched element has no `id`.
2. Close the gate on the retired secret before anything is mutated. Invoke `DrainAction` with the 1-based attempt number; it returns the number of requests still in flight on the current secret. Repeat until it reports zero or `DrainLimit` attempts have been made, waiting `DrainIntervalSeconds` between attempts but never after the last attempt or after a zero. If callers never drain, throw `VcfCredentialDrainTimeoutException` carrying `ResourceName`, `DrainAttempts` and `InFlightCount`, and submit nothing.
3. Build one `CredentialsUpdateSpec` with `operationType` `ROTATE` and a single `ResourceCredentials` element holding a single `BaseCredential`, then submit it with `updateOrRotatePasswords`. Take the task id from the response and reject a blank one.
4. Acceptance is not completion. Read the credentials task with `getCredentialsTask` until it reaches a terminal state, normalising status by trimming, upper-casing invariantly and replacing spaces with underscores. `PENDING` and `IN_PROGRESS` are non-terminal, `SUCCESSFUL` is the successful terminal state, and `FAILED`, `USER_CANCELLED` and `INCONSISTENT` are failed terminal states. Wait `PollIntervalSeconds` between non-terminal reads only, never after a terminal read and never after the last permitted read. `PollLimit` bounds the total number of task reads for the whole rotation, retry included.
5. The first time a task reaches `FAILED`, resubmit the original specification unchanged with `retryCredentialsTask` on the same task id and keep polling. Retry at most once. A second failed terminal state, or any other failed terminal state, throws `VcfCredentialRotationFailedException` carrying `TaskId`, `TaskStatus` (the status string as returned), `ErrorCode` (from the task's first error, empty when absent) and `RetryAttempted`, with the task's first error message as the exception message.
6. If the poll budget is exhausted while the task is still non-terminal, cancel it with `cancelCredentialsTask` so no half-applied secret is left behind, then throw `VcfCredentialRotationTimeoutException` carrying `TaskId`, `PollCount`, `Cancelled` and `CancelStatus` (the status of the cancel response).
7. Only after a `SUCCESSFUL` task, read the rotated credential back with `getCredential` using the id from step 1, require its `username` to match and its `password` to be non-empty, and then invoke `PublishAction` exactly once with that replacement secret. A rotation that failed, was cancelled or never drained publishes nothing and reads nothing back.

On success return one `[pscustomobject]` whose properties are exactly `ResourceName`, `ResourceType`, `Username`, `CredentialId`, `TaskId`, `Status`, `PollCount`, `DrainAttempts`, `RetryAttempted`, `RotatedAt`, in that order. `Status` is the terminal status string as returned, `PollCount` is the number of credentials-task reads, `DrainAttempts` is the number of `DrainAction` invocations, and `RotatedAt` is the read-back `modificationTimestamp`. No returned property and no exception message may contain a password or an access token.

The wire shape is strict, and unset optional fields must be absent rather than sent empty. The lookup carries only the bound filters: `resourceIp`, `domainName`, `pageNumber`, `pageSize`, and an unbound `accountType`, are omitted entirely, never sent blank. `ROTATE` means SDDC Manager generates the replacement, so `BaseCredential.password` is never sent, not even as an empty string; `accountType` appears on the credential only when `-AccountType` was bound; `ResourceCredentials.resourceId` and `CredentialsUpdateSpec.autoRotatePolicy` stay off the wire; and the retry body is the unchanged original specification.

Run `pwsh -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File .protected/verify.ps1`. The protected verifier connects the real SDK to a contract-pinned loopback SDDC Manager on an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` port and reads its fsynced request log. It drives a rotation that drains and succeeds, one that fails and is retried once, one that never finishes and must be cancelled, and one whose callers never drain. It checks the exact ordered operation sequence, targets, query fields, bodies, omitted optionals, retry equality, drain-before-submit and confirm-before-publish ordering, poll and drain bounds, result shape and exception detail. The mock serves only the operations named by the contract plus the SDK connection probe that the contract records, and no live VMware endpoint is contacted. Everything under `.protected/` and `docs/` is protected; edit only `VcfCredentialRotation/VcfCredentialRotation.psm1`.
scenario: a credential rotation drains its in-flight callers before any mutation, polls the credentials task to a terminal state, and publishes the replacement only after a confirmed read-back; a failed task is retried once, an unfinished task is cancelled, and callers that never drain leave the estate untouched
constraint: the contract-pinned loopback service exposes only the seven projected operations plus the SDK connection probe the contract records, and its fsynced request log proves drain-before-submit and confirm-before-publish ordering plus the exact wire shape, including that unset optional query fields, BaseCredential.password, resourceId and autoRotatePolicy are omitted rather than sent empty
